title: Liver disease: cirrhosis, hepatitis C, fatty liver
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's liver disease.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for liver condition.

HPI: 90 y/o male pt presents for routine follow-up of cirrhosis. Pt reports feeling generally well today. Denies any acute abdominal pain, fever, chills, or significant fatigue. Reports stable appetite and activity levels. No new concerns since last visit. Pt is here for monitoring of his chronic liver condition.

Medication List:
- Pantoprazole 40mg PO QD
- Vitamin K 1.0mg PO QD
- Multivitamin daily

Vitals:
BP: 128/76
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 96% on RA
Weight: 165 lbs

Recent Labs:
ALT: 45 U/L
AST: 52 U/L
Albumin: 3.2 g/dL
INR: 1.3
Platelets: 145,000
eGFR: 55 mL/min/1.73m2

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or weight loss.
GI: No nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits.
MSK: No joint pain or stiffness.
Neuro: No confusion or tremors.
CV: No chest pain or palpitations.

Social History: Retired. Lives with wife. Non-smoker. Occasional social drinking.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Exam:
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3. In no acute distress.
CV: RRR, regular rhythm.
Lungs: CTAB, no wheezes or rales.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender. No guarding. No palpable masses.
Skin: No new lesions.
Ext: No edema.

Assessment:
1. Cirrhosis. Stable at this time.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Routine lab work to monitor liver function and coagulation status.
3. Follow up in 3 months for repeat labs and clinical evaluation.
4. Patient instructed to report any acute symptoms or changes in status immediately.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Cirrhosis of the liver with no cause documented: K74.60 (HCC 64).

distractors.why: Alcohol is not documented as the cause.
K74.69 is for other specified cirrhosis; no type is documented.
